Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No credible evidence found after searching World Bank ID4D dataset, UNECA CRVS reports, general web searches for population register, civil register of persons digital. Paper-based civil registration exists but no national digital population register.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 'No' is contradicted by evidence: Décret n°22/07 (2 March 2022) legally established a national General Population File (Fichier Général de la Population, FGP) run by the Office National d'Identification de la Population (ONIP), recording biographic and biometric data. A June 2023 Prime Minister's office ceremony transferred CENI enrolment data/equipment to ONIP and the statistics institute (INS), and ONIP announced (29 May 2026) the launch of a second national identification/ID-card exercise via a public-private partnership. The register has a firm legal basis and active, if incomplete, rollout, but is not yet deployed nationwide, so recoded from 1=No to 3=Under development.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: No credible evidence of digital social protection registers; mentions of social fund lists but no unified digital registry.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 'No' is contradicted by evidence: DRC's Council of Ministers adopted (25 July 2025) and the government enacted (Décret n°25/041, 4 December 2025) a Registre Social Unique (RSU), a socio-economic database centralising biographic, biometric and programme data for social-protection targeting, building on a World Bank-financed beneficiary database (STEP project) that had already registered over 1.8 million individuals by c.2020. Implementation was disrupted by the 2023 dissolution of the delivery agency FSRDC (350,000 beneficiaries temporarily lost cash transfers). The register is legally established and under active build-out but not yet unified/operational nationwide, so recoded from 1=No to 3=Under development.
